question.text: Let a parabola <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> be such that its vertex and focus lie on the positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> units from the origin, respectively. If tangents are drawn from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> to the parabola <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> which meet <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math>, then the area (in sq. units) of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>S</mi><mi>O</mi><mi>R</mi></math> is equal to :

solution.text:
From the diagram, clearly RS is latus-rectum

∵ VF=4-22+0-02=2=a

∴ RS=4a=8

Now OF=2a=4

So, the area of triangle ORS=12×4×8=16
